host: Claude Agent SDK (Python) with Claude Code
covers: every tool call Claude Code reports to the PreToolUse hook of options wrapped by GroundedAgentAdapter.wrap_options(), including tools in allowed_tools
does_not_cover: a tool's own nested calls (an MCP tool calling another service); calls of a session whose options were not wrapped
scope: this adapter instance: every session and subagent it serves, ordered by its lock; serve sessions that must not share records with separate adapters
boundaries: Stop of any session this adapter serves (its main agent's turn ends)
UserPromptSubmit of any session this adapter serves (a turn starts, which also ends what a turn left when its Stop never came)

prompt_configurations: Claude Code permission mode default, acceptEdits or plan: the PreToolUse hook answers ask and can_use_tool, or the permission prompt tool, decides; in any other mode the call is refused with F502

concurrency_note: CheckpointTracker's lock makes a check, a hold and its use one atomic step; a hold is re-checked and used in one step when the call is allowed
host_gaps: The PreToolUse matcher sets on_failure "block", so a callback that fails or gives no verdict in time, as the CLI sees it, blocks the call, and the SDK refuses to connect to a Claude Code that does not honour it; a claude-agent-sdk whose HookMatcher has no on_failure cannot ask for it (the adapter logs a warning), and there such a callback is no decision and the call runs

With a permission_prompt_tool_name, a call the prompt tool refuses is not reported to the adapter: the checkpoint it held is lost (it counts as used when its hold lapses or the session's turn ends), so the next gated call needs a new checkpoint

The permission mode is read from the hook input, else from the wrapped options: a host that changes the mode during a session and omits it from hook input is checked against the mode the session started in
That Claude Code puts an ask to can_use_tool in modes default, acceptEdits and plan rests on its documentation; the tests call the hook and the callback directly
strict_mode=False, approval='off', check_outputs=False or create_grounded_mcp_server(require_layer=False) is outside class SL

§4.4.2 and §5.18.4, destination policies: the adapter does not see a tool's nested calls, so while a destination policy is in force it refuses with F504 every call of a composite whose invokes reach, transitively, a binding that performs send, wherever that send would go
calls_without_output: §5.18.10 output-contract row, §5.20 hosts outside a workflow and §5.21.3's minimum confidence: the adapter receives a capability output from every MCP tool bound to a capability, whose result carries it as the I-JSON text of the output object, its one text content item (§5.18.9), and checks the text the session reads against the capability's output contract (R402), then GroundedAgentConfig.grounding and the applied profiles' grounding policies (F505) and their minimum confidence (F504): a tool create_grounded_mcp_server serves checks its own result (with require_layer; the SDK's server delivers a result's content and is_error, not its structuredContent), and the PostToolUse hook checks the result of any other, as Claude Code passes it, and replaces a refused result with the refusal (updatedMCPToolOutput). Claude Code's own tools (Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, Bash, ...) return results in their own forms, which carry no capability output, so no output check applies to their calls and their results are passed on as they are. The adapter logs a warning, once per tool, when a policy requires the capability of such a call or a profile sets a minimum confidence
